1.8.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation explicitly includes trafficking as a covered category for children under Pasal 13 ayat (1) huruf h: "Anak korban penculikan, penjualan, dan/atau perdagangan" (children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, and/or trafficking). This is substantive coverage in the operative articles, not merely a preamble reference. Although the retrieved candidates did not include Pasal 13(1)(h), they did include the preamble listing UU 21/2007 (anti-trafficking) and PP 9/2008 (integrated services for trafficking victims). Given the document’s title and broad scope, and especially the explicit legal basis referencing trafficking-specific instruments, a judge could reasonably infer trafficking is within scope; however the strongest ground-truth basis is Pasal 13(1)(h) which the judge did not see. Still, the judge’s rationale that trafficking is not included is incorrect relative to the actual regulation.

This indicates services should be delivered by trained personnel, but it does not establish any policy commitment to provide training/capacity-building programs (i.e., no mandate to conduct training, build capacity, allocate training resources, or implement training plans). The judge treated the existence of 'trained officers' as equivalent to a training/capacity-building mechanism, which is an overbroad inference. PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION.
The purpose of the establishment of the State is stated in the fourth paragraph of the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "The State protects all Indonesian people and all Indonesian territory and to promote general welfare, educate the life of the nation and participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice". The meaning of protecting here includes protecting every citizen including from all forms of violence. In addition, Article 28 G paragraph 2 of the 1945 Constitution states that every person has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity. Thus the right to obtain protection from acts of violence is guaranteed by the constitution.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights. Women and children victims of violence must have their dignity and honor protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buleleng Regency, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.
Protection of women and children victims of violence in the Region requires institutional and regulatory support that can guarantee its implementation. The Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims specifically in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Buleleng Regency.

6.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text does not identify 'trafficking victims' as a specific intersectional/vulnerable group for women; the explicit trafficking-related vulnerable group appears for children in Pasal 13 ayat (1) huruf h ("Anak korban ... perdagangan"). The judge relied on the elucidation of Pasal 5 huruf b that sexual violence includes "pemaksaan hubungan seksual dengan orang lain untuk tujuan komersial" (forced sex with another person for commercial purposes). That describes a form of sexual violence/exploitation, but it is not the same as explicitly covering trafficking victims as a target group (and it is not framed as 'victims of trafficking' or 'perdagangan orang'). Since the retrieved passages did not contain Pasal 13(1)(h) and the cited snippet does not establish trafficking-victim targeting, the judge’s conclusion (Yes) is a category error/overreach.
